items.summary: Effective January 24, 2024, the Ministry of Finance amended the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019, to establish a framework enabling public Indian companies to directly list and issue ordinary shares on international exchanges located in permitted jurisdictions like GIFT-IFSC. The rules apply to unlisted and listed public Indian companies, their existing shareholders, and eligible foreign holders, subject to specific regulatory eligibility criteria, pricing mechanisms, and anti-money laundering compliance.

items.title: Consultation paper on proposal to enhance trust in the Alternative Investment Funds (‘AIF’) ecosystem to facilitate Ease of Doing Business measures
items.summary: SEBI proposes amending the AIF Regulations, 2012, to mandate that AIFs, their managers, and key management personnel conduct specific pre-investment due diligence to ensure investments do not facilitate the circumvention of any financial sector regulations, with non-compliant investor participation requiring either investment withdrawal or investor exclusion. This obligation applies to all Alternative Investment Funds, their managers, and key management personnel. Public comments on this proposal must be submitted by February 11, 2024.

items.title: Guidelines for AIFs with respect to holding their investments in dematerialised form and appointment of custodian
items.summary: This SEBI circular mandates that all Alternative Investment Funds must hold their investments in dematerialized form for any fresh investments made from October 1, 2024, onwards, while imposing the same requirement by January 31, 2025, on prior investments where the investee company is legally mandated to dematerialize or where the AIF and other regulated intermediaries exercise control. Furthermore, Category I and II AIF schemes with a corpus of up to INR 500 crore that already held investments as of January 12, 2024, as well as AIFs utilizing associate custodians, must appoint a registered custodian and comply with related regulations by January 31, 2025. Managers and custodians are also required to adopt upcoming implementation standards for reporting custody data, incorporate compliance into their quarterly filings and Compliance Test Reports, and ensure new schemes appoint a custodian prior to making their first investment.

items.title: Consultation Paper on providing flexibility to Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) and their investors to deal with unliquidated investments of their schemes beyond expiry of tenure
items.summary: SEBI is proposing amendments to allow Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) to manage unliquidated investments via a "Dissolution Period" upon obtaining a 75% investor consent threshold and arranging a 25% portfolio bid, replacing the previous requirement to launch a separate liquidation scheme. This framework applies to registered AIF managers, their schemes, legacy AIFs whose liquidation periods expired prior to June 15, 2023 (granting them a fresh one-year liquidation period), and erstwhile VCFs transitioning to the AIF regime. The consultation paper invites public comments, but the text truncates before specifying the final compliance submission deadline.

items.title: Foreign investment in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: SEBI has updated its AIF Master Circular to align beneficial ownership criteria with recent amendments to the Prevention of Money Laundering Rules, prohibiting AIFs from accepting capital contributions from investors or beneficial owners linked to UNSC sanctions lists or high-risk FATF jurisdictions. This restriction applies to all registered Alternative Investment Funds and immediately halts capital drawdowns from any existing or newly on-boarded investors who fail to satisfy these revised screening standards, effective from January 11, 2024.

items.title: Credit of units of AIFs in dematerialised form
items.summary: SEBI has established a procedural framework allowing Alternative Investment Funds to credit units to an "Aggregate Escrow Demat Account" for investors who have failed to submit their demat particulars, pending subsequent transfer to the investors' actual accounts once details are furnished. This mandate applies to all AIFs, fund managers, depositories, and custodians, with compliance deadlines set for January 31, 2024, for schemes with a corpus of INR 500 crores or more, and May 10, 2024, for schemes with a corpus under INR 500 crores.

items.title: Consultation Paper on changes in the regulatory framework for Special Situation Funds, a sub-category of Category I Alternative Investment Funds, necessary to facilitate Special Situation Funds to acquire stressed loans in terms of Reserve Bank of India (Transfer of Loan Exposures) Directions, 2021
items.summary: This consultation paper proposes amendments to the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 to align the regulatory framework for Special Situation Funds (SSFs) with the Reserve Bank of India's Master Directions on Transfer of Loan Exposures, enabling SSFs to acquire stressed loans. The proposed changes apply to all SSFs, their managers, sponsors, and investors, introducing stricter eligibility checks, expanded conflict-of-interest restrictions, post-lock-in transfer limitations, and mandatory reporting obligations. The document does not specify a final implementation deadline as it is currently open for public feedback.

items.title: Consultation Paper on Regulatory Framework for Accredited Investors in IFSC
items.summary: This IFSCA consultation paper proposes a formal regulatory framework for identifying, onboarding, and reviewing Accredited Investors in the International Financial Services Centre, setting specific financial thresholds such as an annual income of USD 200,000 or net assets of USD 1 million for individuals. It applies to regulated entities—including fund management entities and intermediaries—that accept or distribute products to such investors, requiring them to establish internal verification policies, maintain records for at least ten years, and secure written acknowledgments regarding reduced investor protections and voluntary consent. The document was published on November 23, 2023, for public comments and does not specify a final compliance deadline or effective date.

items.title: Seeking suggestions towards review of IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022
items.summary: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) has invited public comments and recommendations from regulated entities and stakeholders to comprehensively review the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022, in line with Union Budget directives to ease compliance. Submissions must be emailed in MS Word or MS Excel format using a prescribed template to designated Authority officials by October 31, 2023.

items.title: IFSCA constitutes Fund Management Advisory Committee (FMAC)
items.summary: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) has established a standing Fund Management Advisory Committee, chaired by former RBI Deputy Governor N S Vishwanathan, to guide the growth, product innovation, and regulation of the fund management sector in IFSCs. Comprising industry leaders, legal and tax experts, and former regulators, the committee is tasked with formulating long-term development plans, benchmarking the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022 against global standards, and identifying potential market malpractices. The press release issued on September 27, 2023, does not specify any operational deadlines or direct compliance requirements for market participants.

items.title: Regulatory Reporting by AIFs
items.summary: SEBI has introduced a revised quarterly reporting format for Alternative Investment Funds to standardise compliance and facilitate regulatory oversight, developed in consultation with industry associations like IVCA and Equalifi. The updated reports must be filed online through the SEBI Intermediary Portal within 15 calendar days from the end of each quarter. As part of the rollout timeline, a trial run for the June 2023 quarter is mandated by October 15, 2023, the report for the September 30, 2023 quarter is due by November 15, 2023, and regular compliance under the new format commences for the quarter ending December 31, 2023.

items.title: Notification of investment trust, scheme and ETF under section 47(viiab) of Income Tax Act, 1961
items.summary: The Central Board of Direct Taxes has amended Notification No. 16/2020 to include units of investment trusts, schemes, and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) launched under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022, within the scope of specified capital assets under section 47(viiab) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. This amendment applies to relevant entities and transactions involving these specific units in IFSC-domiciled funds. The notification comes into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette on September 12, 2023.

items.title: Validity period of approval granted by SEBI to Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) for overseas investment
items.summary: SEBI has reduced the validity period for making approved overseas investments from six months to four months to ensure more efficient utilization of allocated limits within the industry. This update applies to all registered Alternative Investment Funds and erstwhile Venture Capital Funds seeking offshore investment approvals. The revised four-month timeline takes effect for all overseas investment approvals granted by SEBI on or after August 4, 2023.

items.title: Amendment to CBDT notification 55/2019 to include funds regulated by IFSCA
items.summary: The Central Board of Direct Taxes amended Notification No. 55/2019 to expand the definition of an "investment fund" under Section 139(1C) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, ensuring that Category I and Category II funds regulated by the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022 are now included alongside SEBI-regulated AIFs. This inclusion applies to investment funds established or incorporated in India as a trust, company, limited liability partnership, or body corporate. The notification came into force immediately upon its publication in the Official Gazette on July 14, 2023.

items.title: Clarification regarding taxability of income earned by a non-resident investor from off-shore investments routed through Category I or II AIF
items.summary: This Central Board of Direct Taxes circular updates earlier tax guidelines to incorporate the International Financial Services Centres Authority (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022, following amendments made by the Finance Act of 2023. Consequently, the tax pass-through regime under section 115UB of the Income-tax Act, 1961, now formally extends to Category I and Category II Alternative Investment Funds regulated by either SEBI or the IFSCA. The clarification takes effect immediately upon its issuance on July 12, 2023, and applies to non-resident investors routing offshore investments through these qualifying funds.

items.title: Standardised approach to valuation of investment portfolio of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: This SEBI circular establishes a standardized valuation framework for Alternative Investment Funds, requiring them to follow Mutual Fund norms or industry association guidelines, appoint independent valuers meeting specific eligibility criteria, and adhere to strict disclosure mandates for valuation deviations and methodology changes. It applies to all SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds, their managers, sponsors, and trustees. The provisions take effect on November 1, 2023, with specific requirements for reporting audited investee data to performance benchmarking agencies within stipulated timelines.

items.title: Modalities for launching Liquidation Scheme and for distributing the investments of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) in-specie
items.summary: SEBI has established operational modalities under the June 15, 2023 AIF Regulations amendments enabling Alternative Investment Funds to launch Liquidation Schemes or execute in-specie distributions for unliquidated assets during a scheme's one-year liquidation period, requiring 75% investor consent by value, a mandatory 25% minimum bid arrangement for exit options, and specific valuation frameworks for manager track records. This circular applies to all Alternative Investment Funds, their managers, trustees, and key management personnel, and comes into force with immediate effect from June 21, 2023.

items.title: Consultation paper on proposal with respect to pro-rata and pari-passu rights of investors of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: This consultation paper proposes amending the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, to explicitly mandate that AIFs maintain pro-rata and pari-passu rights for investors across all investments and distributions, thereby effectively restricting priority distribution and tranching models. These proposed requirements would apply directly to all Alternative Investment Funds, their managers, sponsors, and investors, particularly targeting structures that risk regulatory arbitrage or ever-greening of loans. While an interim circular issued on November 23, 2022, immediately halted affected AIF schemes from accepting fresh commitments or making new investments pending a final regulatory decision, this consultation paper seeks public and stakeholder inputs without specifying a final implementation deadline.

items.title: Consultation Paper on the proposal to review Qualified Institutional Buyer status of Alternative Investment Funds, Venture Capital Funds and Foreign Venture Capital Investors
items.summary: SEBI has proposed tightening Qualified Institutional Buyer (QIB) eligibility criteria to prevent regulatory arbitrage by closely held vehicles. Under the proposal, Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) where a single investor or a group of related parties contribute 50% or more, alongside Foreign Venture Capital Investors (FVCIs) structured as corporate bodies or family offices, will lose their QIB status. Public comments on these proposed amendments are invited until June 1, 2023.

items.title: Consultation paper on proposed amendment to SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 to strengthen governance mechanisms of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: This consultation paper proposes tightening AIF governance by restricting Category I and II funds from borrowing for investments—allowing it only in emergencies for drawdown shortfalls up to ten percent with a thirty-day cooling-off period—and mandating that all AIFs hold their portfolio securities exclusively in dematerialized form. It applies to all Alternative Investment Funds, Category I and II AIF managers, and sponsors, while introducing a six-month compliance timeline for dematerializing existing investments where funds hold a controlling interest.

items.title: Direct plan for schemes of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and trail model for distribution commission in AIFs
items.summary: SEBI has mandated that all Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) schemes must introduce a Direct Plan without any distribution or placement fees, and requires investors using SEBI-registered intermediaries that charge separate advisory or portfolio management fees to be compulsorily on-boarded through these Direct Plans. Furthermore, the circular enforces a trail model for distribution commissions, prohibiting upfront fees entirely for Category III AIFs—where commissions must be paid solely on an equal trail basis out of the manager's management fee—while permitting Category I and II AIFs to pay a maximum of one-third upfront and the rest as an equal trail over the fund's tenure. These compliance requirements apply to all AIFs and their schemes with respect to investors on-boarded from May 1, 2023 onwards.

items.title: Consultation Paper on Handling of Client Funds for Portfolio Management Services in IFSC
items.summary: The International Financial Services Centres Authority has proposed amending Regulation 77(2) of the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022, to grant Fund Management Entities providing Portfolio Management Services greater flexibility in handling client funds. Under the proposed framework, clients may maintain their funds in a specific account with an IFSC Banking Unit, a bank in India, or a foreign jurisdiction, provided the Fund Management Entity is authorized to operate the account and can furnish transactional details to the regulator upon request. Stakeholders and the public were invited to submit their comments and suggestions on these proposed amendments by March 8, 2023.

items.title: Consultation paper on review of eligibility criteria for the key investment team and prescribing qualification for compliance officer of Manager of an Alternative Investment Fund
items.summary: SEBI has proposed amending the Alternative Investment Fund Regulations, 2012 to remove the mandatory five-year experience requirement for the key investment team of an AIF manager and replace it, alongside introducing a new regulatory qualification mandate for AIF compliance officers, with specific certification requirements from notified institutions. These proposed changes apply directly to managers of all registered Alternative Investment Funds, who were required to submit their public comments on these proposals by February 18, 2023.

items.title: Consultation paper on direct plan for schemes of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and trail model for distribution commission in AIFs
items.summary: SEBI has proposed mandating Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) to offer zero-distribution-fee direct plans, requiring investors using fee-charging intermediaries like Investment Advisers or Portfolio Managers to use this route with adjusted unit allocations for equal NAVs. Additionally, the consultation paper proposes replacing upfront commissions with a full trail model for Category III AIFs, while permitting Category I and II AIFs to pay up to one-third of the total distribution fee upfront in the first year with the remainder on a trail basis. Stakeholders and market participants were invited to submit public comments on these proposals by February 18, 2023.

items.title: Consultation paper on dematerialisation of units of AIFs
items.summary: SEBI proposes to mandate the dematerialisation of all Alternative Investment Fund units in a phased manner, starting with schemes having a corpus exceeding INR 500 crores by April 1, 2024. While electronic holding will become compulsory, fund managers will retain control over unit transfers through private placement memorandums and investor agreements. This requirement applies to AIF managers, funds, and their investors, with public comments invited until February 18, 2023.

items.title: Consultation paper on Investor consent for buying/selling investments from/to associates of AIFs
items.summary: SEBI proposes to mandate that Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) must secure approval from at least 75% of investors by investment value before purchasing or selling portfolio investments involving associates or related AIF schemes managed by the same Sponsor, Manager, or their affiliates. This requirement directly impacts all registered AIF managers, sponsors, and compliance officers structuring secondary transactions or cross-trades within fund groups. Public comments on this consultation paper are invited by February 18, 2023.

items.title: Consultation Paper on providing option to Alternative Investment Funds and their investors to carry forward unliquidated investments of a scheme upon completion of its tenure
items.summary: SEBI has issued a consultation paper proposing a framework that allows Alternative Investment Funds and Large Value Funds to transfer unliquidated scheme assets into a new scheme upon tenure expiry, subject to a 75% investor consent threshold by value. To ensure transparent valuation and liquidity, managers must secure third-party bids for at least 25% of the unliquidated portfolio to provide pro-rata exits, or alternatively rely on Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code liquidation values. Public comments on these proposed rules must be submitted in the specified format by February 18, 2023.

items.title: Transaction in Corporate Bonds through Request for Quote (RFQ) platform by Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: SEBI has mandated that all Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) must execute a minimum of 10% of their total monthly secondary market trades in corporate bonds by value through the Request for Quote (RFQ) platform. Additionally, any corporate bond transactions where AIFs are present on both sides must be carried out via the RFQ platform in 'one-to-one' mode, with specific counting rules applicable to 'one-to-many' trades executed between AIFs. These compliance requirements become effective on April 1, 2023.

items.title: Consultation Paper on standardised approach to valuation of investment portfolio of Alternative Investment Funds
items.summary: This consultation paper proposes mandatory adoption of International Private Equity and Venture Capital Valuation Guidelines (IPEV Guidelines) and specific Mutual Fund valuation norms for all Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) to standardise portfolio valuation. It applies to AIF managers, sponsors, and trustees across Category I, II, and III AIFs, introducing strict eligibility criteria for independent valuers—including IBBI registration, relevant professional memberships, and at least three years of unlisted security valuation experience. Additionally, the proposals establish specific compliance timelines for reporting audited scheme valuation data to performance benchmarking agencies.

items.title: Foreign investment in Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: SEBI has mandated that AIF managers must ensure foreign investors originate from jurisdictions whose regulators are IOSCO MMoU Appendix A signatories or have a bilateral MoU with SEBI, with an exception for specific government-related investors approved by the Government of India. Furthermore, managers must verify that neither the investors nor their controllers or significant contributors (holding 25% or more) are listed on UNSC sanctions lists or reside in high-risk FATF jurisdictions, and must immediately halt capital drawdowns from any non-compliant investors already on-boarded. This circular applies to all Alternative Investment Funds and came into force with immediate effect on December 9, 2022.

items.title: IFSCA (FinTech Incentive) Scheme 2022_Gazette Notification
items.summary: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (FinTech Incentive) Scheme, 2022, effective from February 2, 2022, for an initial operational period of three years, provides financial grants ranging from 10 lakh to 75 lakh rupees to eligible domestic and foreign FinTech entities operating within the IFSC. The scheme covers various forms of financial assistance such as start-up, proof of concept, sandbox, green FinTech, accelerator, and listing support grants, subject to rigorous evaluation, milestone-based disbursements, and compliance conditions including a commitment not to deploy successful solutions in other jurisdictions for three years. Beneficiaries must incorporate an entity in the IFSC upon successfully completing their sandbox or accelerator programs and comply with regulatory requirements or face a simple interest penalty of 8 percent per annum for non-compliance.

items.title: Guidelines for overseas investment by Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) / Venture Capital Funds (VCFs)
items.summary: This SEBI circular applies to all Alternative Investment Funds and erstwhile Venture Capital Funds, establishing streamlined guidelines and application formats for making overseas investments. It removes the previous requirement for target companies to have an Indian connection, while restricting investments to jurisdictions with IOSCO-compliant regulators and excluding FATF-blacklisted or deficient countries. Effective immediately from August 17, 2022, funds must report future divestments within 3 working days and submit historical divestment records within 30 days.

items.title: Guidelines for Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors under SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 and Requirement of Compliance Officer for Managers of all AIFs
items.summary: This circular outlines the operational framework for Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors (LVFs), permitting them to launch schemes under intimation without prior SEBI review via a merchant banker, provided specific due diligence undertakings are submitted. It mandates that close-ended LVFs must clearly define tenure extension terms in their fund documents and secure governing body approval at least one month prior to expiry. Additionally, all AIF managers are required to designate a dedicated compliance officer—distinct from the CEO—to oversee regulatory adherence, with existing LVF filings needing compliance via undertakings by July 31, 2022.

items.title: Change in control of Sponsor and/or Manager of Alternative Investment Fund involving scheme of arrangement under Companies Act, 2013
items.summary: This SEBI circular establishes a streamlined procedure for Alternative Investment Funds seeking regulatory approval for a change in control of their Sponsor or Manager through a Companies Act scheme of arrangement requiring National Company Law Tribunal sanction. Under the new process, funds must apply to SEBI for an in-principle approval prior to approaching the tribunal, maintain a three-month validity window to file before the tribunal, and submit final approval documentation within 15 days of the tribunal's order. These requirements apply to all AIF Sponsor and Manager change-in-control applications involving schemes of arrangement filed with the National Company Law Tribunal on or after April 1, 2022.

items.title: Consultation Paper on Proposed IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022
items.summary: The consultation paper proposes the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022 to establish a unified registration and comprehensive regulatory framework for fund management entities operating in International Financial Services Centres, covering retail schemes, alternative investment funds, portfolio management, exchange-traded funds, ESG strategies, family offices, and special situation funds. It applies to fund managers, investment trusts, and prospective market participants wishing to establish fund operations within an IFSC. Public comments on the draft regulations are invited by February 28, 2022, with the final rules slated to come into force on the thirtieth day following their official publication.

items.title: Clarifications regarding amendment to SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012
items.summary: This SEBI circular clarifies implementation details following the November 9, 2021, amendments to the AIF Regulations, specifically governing concentration norms for Category III AIFs and co-investment frameworks. It applies to all Alternative Investment Funds, their managers, sponsors, and investors, establishing that listed equity concentration limits for Category III AIFs must be computed using the NAV of the fund from the preceding business day. Furthermore, passive breaches of these concentration limits must be rectified within 30 days, and the mandatory custodian requirement applies if the combined corpus of the AIF and co-investments managed via a Co-investment Portfolio Manager exceeds 500 crore rupees.

items.title: Modalities for filing of placement memorandum through a Merchant Banker under SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012
items.summary: This SEBI circular mandates that all Alternative Investment Funds must file their placement memorandums—as well as annual consolidated changes to them—through an independent SEBI-registered Merchant Banker who is not an associate of the fund, its sponsor, manager, or trustee. The Merchant Banker is required to independently verify all disclosures and submit a detailed due diligence certificate along with specific compliance annexures. These new filing and due diligence requirements become effective on November 11, 2021, which is the ninety-first day following the August 13, 2021 amendments to the AIF Regulations.

items.title: Circular on Amendment to SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012
items.summary: This SEBI circular, issued on June 25, 2021, applies to all Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and permits them to simultaneously invest in direct securities and units of other AIFs without being labelled as a "Fund of AIFs," subject to updating Private Placement Memorandums and obtaining consent from at least two-thirds of unitholders by value. It further clarifies that Category III AIFs investing in other AIFs can take on leverage up to two times their Net Asset Value (excluding the value of those underlying AIF units), mandates that key management personnel abide by the Code of Conduct under the AIF Regulations, and sets out the required format for investor waivers regarding Investment Committees alongside rules on changing ex-officio external members. The circular does not specify a distinct implementation deadline, meaning the compliance requirements apply with immediate effect following the May 5, 2021 underlying regulation amendments.

items.title: Enhancement of overall limit for overseas investment by Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)/Venture Capital Funds (VCFs)
items.summary: SEBI has doubled the aggregate overseas investment limit for Alternative Investment Funds and legacy Venture Capital Funds from USD 750 million to USD 1,500 million, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India. This update applies to all registered AIFs and VCFs seeking to make offshore investments, while all other existing regulatory conditions and compliance terms remain unchanged. The circular came into effect immediately upon its issuance on May 21, 2021, without prescribing any separate transition timeline.

items.title: Clarifications with respect to Circular dated February 05, 2020 on ‘Disclosure Standards for Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: This SEBI circular applies to all Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and introduces key clarifications and deadline extensions regarding the February 5, 2020 disclosure standards. It mandates that the annual Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) compliance audit must be completed and submitted to the governing bodies, trustees, and SEBI within six months of the financial year-end, though AIFs with zero raised funds need only submit a Chartered Accountant certificate confirming this status. Additionally, the threshold for an AIF association to notify benchmarking agencies is adjusted to represent at least 33% of AIFs, the deadline for FY 2019-20 compliance is pushed to December 31, 2020, and the timeline for releasing the first industry and AIF performance benchmarks is extended to October 1, 2020.

items.title: Special Economic Zone(4th Amendment) Rules, 2019 - Exemption to Alternate Invesment Fund & Mutual Funds
items.summary: The Special Economic Zones (4th Amendment) Rules, 2019, exempt Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) and Mutual Funds set up as units in an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) from specific Net Foreign Exchange (NFE) restrictions regarding investor inflows, investments, and returns, while also providing a formula to combine the unit's NFE with its fund manager's. Additionally, the rules exempt IFSC Insurance Offices for certain premium incomes and related investments, subject to IRDAI guidelines. These amendments came into force immediately upon their publication in the Official Gazette on December 31, 2019.

items.title: Consultation Paper on Introduction of Performance Benchmarking and Standardization of Private Placement Memorandum for Alternative Investment Funds
items.summary: SEBI's consultation paper proposes mandating performance benchmarking for Alternative Investment Funds registered for at least three years—requiring them to submit audited scheme-level cash flow and valuation data to recognized benchmarking agencies on a half-yearly basis—while also introducing standardized Private Placement Memorandum templates and an annual compliance audit of PPM terms focusing on side letters. These requirements apply to all SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds, their managers, and applicants referencing past performance data, with public comments invited until December 25, 2019.

items.title: Exemption from filing return of income for investors of Category I and II AIF in IFSC
Overseas Investment by Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) / Venture Capital Funds (VCFs)
items.summary: This SEBI circular increases the aggregate overseas investment limit for Alternative Investment Funds and erstwhile Venture Capital Funds from USD 500 million to USD 750 million, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India. It mandates that funds report any limit utilization within 5 working days on the SEBI intermediary portal, and requires reporting within 2 working days of the expiry of the 6-month validity period for any unutilized or partially unutilized limits, or upon a voluntary decision to surrender the limit. The provisions of this circular became applicable on July 2, 2018.

items.title: Filing of Term Sheet by Angel Funds
SEBI introduces Online System for Portfolio Managers and Venture Capital Funds
items.summary: SEBI has launched a centralized online portal at https://siportal.sebi.gov.in on May 30, 2017, to streamline regulatory compliance, registration, and reporting processes. This digital mandate applies to all prospective and existing SEBI-registered Portfolio Managers under the 1993 Regulations as well as Venture Capital Funds governed by the 1996 Regulations. While no specific compliance deadline is mentioned in the release, existing entities have been individually notified via email to activate their online accounts and utilize the portal's integrated user manual and helpline for assistance.

items.title: Consultation Paper on permitting Category III Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) in the commodity derivatives market
items.summary: SEBI's consultation paper proposes permitting Category III Alternative Investment Funds to participate as clients in the Indian commodity derivatives market to enhance liquidity and price discovery, subject to a single-commodity investment cap of ten percent of investable funds, existing leverage limits of two times NAV, and mandatory investor disclosures and consent. The framework applies to Category III AIF managers and compliance officers, with public comments invited until May 20, 2017.

items.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.
items.summary: This SEBI FAQ document clarifies regulatory provisions under the 2012 AIF Regulations, setting out mandatory parameters for market participants such as fund managers, sponsors, and investors establishing alternative investment funds in India. It requires general AIF schemes to maintain a minimum corpus of 20 crore rupees (10 crore rupees for angel funds), enforce a minimum ticket size of 1 crore rupees per investor (25 lakh rupees for employees, directors, and angel investors), and maintain continuing sponsor or manager interest capped at specified lesser percentages of the corpus or absolute monetary thresholds depending on the fund category. Compliance timelines dictate that quarterly reports must be emailed within 7 calendar days of each quarter-end for Category I and II AIFs and unleveraged Category III AIFs, while leveraged Category III AIFs must submit monthly reports within 7 calendar days of month-end, and scheme fees of 1 lakh rupees must be paid at least 30 days prior to launching any subsequent scheme.

items.title: Consultative Paper On Guidelines On Overseas Investments And Other Issues/Clarifications For AIFs/VCFs
items.summary: This SEBI consultation paper proposes expanding overseas investment limits for both legacy Venture Capital Funds (VCFs) and SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) to 25% of a scheme's investible funds, subject to a combined industry-wide cap of USD 500 million and a mandatory "Indian connection" requirement for target offshore companies. It applies to all registered AIFs, VCFs, fund managers, trustees, and sponsors, introducing new operational mandates such as calculating scheme tenure from the final closing date, limiting associate disciplinary disclosures in placement memoranda to the top 20 associates by turnover, and enforcing strict fiduciary duties and scheme-wise account segregation. Public comments on these proposed guidelines are invited by May 7, 2015, with approved overseas investments required to be utilized within a strict 6-month validity window from the date of SEBI's prior approval on a first-come, first-served basis.

items.title: Amendments to SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012
items.summary: SEBI has amended the Alternative Investment Funds Regulations, 2012, to establish a formal registration and compliance framework for "Angel Funds" as a sub-category under Category I Venture Capital Funds, alongside permitting Social Venture Funds to collect grants from providers without returning profits. The new angel fund framework applies to angel investors—requiring individuals to possess specific early-stage experience or senior management backgrounds and a minimum net tangible asset of Rs. 2 crore, or corporate bodies with a Rs. 10 crore net worth—and mandates that angel funds maintain a corpus of at least Rs. 10 crore, accept a minimum investment of Rs. 25 lakhs per investor (payable over up to 3 years), and invest between Rs. 50 lakhs and Rs. 5 crore in eligible young enterprises for a mandatory 3-year lock-in. The press release does not specify a separate effective date or transitional timeline beyond notifying the amendments.

items.title: Circular for Operational, Prudential and Reporting Norms for Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs)
items.summary: SEBI has introduced operational, prudential, and reporting standards for Alternative Investment Funds through a circular dated July 29, 2013. The framework mandates quarterly reporting for Category I and II AIFs as well as unleveraged Category III AIFs, while leveraged Category III AIFs must report monthly and restrict their gross exposure to a maximum of two times their net asset value. Additionally, Category III AIFs employing leverage are subject to specific risk management, compliance, and redemption norms.

items.title: A consent order in respect of M/s ' Small is beautiful' Fund  a Venture Capital Fund (VCF)
items.summary: This SEBI consent order settles enforcement proceedings against the Venture Capital Fund, M/s Small is Beautiful, regarding investments made in associated companies between 2005 and 2007 in violation of Regulations 12(c) and 12(d)(ii) of the SEBI (Venture Capital Funds) Regulations, 1996. To resolve the matter, the fund paid settlement charges of Rs. 37,50,000 via demand drafts dated September 13, 2012. The order came into immediate effect on November 1, 2012, while preserving SEBI's right to take future enforcement action if any representations are found untrue or consent terms are breached.

items.title: SEBI notifies SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations 2012
items.summary: SEBI notified the Alternative Investment Funds Regulations 2012 on May 21, 2012, requiring all pooled investment vehicles such as private equity, real estate, and hedge funds to register under a three-tiered category system with mandatory minimum corpus thresholds of Rs. 20 crores and minimum investor commitments of Rs. 1 crore. The framework repeals the 1996 Venture Capital Fund regulations—allowing existing VCFs to run until maturity without corpus increases or re-register with a 66.67% investor approval—while restricting unregistered legacy funds from floating new schemes or rolling over existing ones without compliance. Additionally, the regulations mandate sponsor "skin in the game" between 2.5% to 5% (capped at Rs. 5 crores or Rs. 10 crores depending on the fund category) and impose strict concentration limits alongside a minimum three-year tenure for close-ended vehicles.

items.title: Concept Paper on proposed Alternative Investment Funds Regulation for Public Comments
items.summary: SEBI has released a concept paper and draft regulations to introduce a dedicated regulatory framework for alternative investment funds, inviting public feedback on the proposed rules. The consultation applies to market participants and stakeholders interested in the governance of alternative investment funds in India. The source text does not specify any deadline, effective date, or compliance timeline for submitting comments.

items.title: Concept Paper On Proposed Alternative Investment Funds Regulation
items.summary: This SEBI consultation paper proposes a comprehensive regulatory framework for Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) such as private equity and real estate funds to replace the outdated 1996 Venture Capital Fund regulations and address systemic financial risks. It applies to private pools of capital, fund managers, and venture capital funds operating in India. The document invites public comments on the concept paper, though it does not specify a final compliance deadline or effective date.

items.title: Revised quarterly reporting format for Venture Capital Funds
items.summary: This SEBI circular prescribes a revised reporting format for quarterly venture capital activity and mandates all registered Venture Capital Funds to submit their compliance reports through the online SEBI portal within seven days from the end of each calendar quarter. The updated reporting framework takes effect starting from the quarter ended March 31, 2010, replacing physical submissions entirely with digital uploads.

items.title: Guidelines for Overseas Investments by Venture Capital Funds
items.summary: SEBI has established an application and approval framework allowing registered venture capital funds to invest up to 10 percent of their investible funds in equity and equity-linked instruments of unlisted offshore venture capital undertakings possessing an Indian operational connection. These overseas investments operate under a cumulative industry limit of USD 500 million allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, requiring participating funds to execute their approved investments within a strict six-month validity window. The guidelines apply directly to all venture capital funds registered with SEBI under the 1996 Regulations seeking cross-border exposure without requiring separate regulatory clearances from the Reserve Bank of India.

items.title: Common Key Personnel between Mutual Funds and Venture Capital Funds
items.summary: SEBI prohibits key personnel of mutual funds from simultaneously serving on the board or investment committees of venture capital fund asset managers, advisors, or investment managers to prevent conflicts of interest. This restriction applies to all venture capital funds registered with SEBI and includes key personnel such as chief executive officers, chief investment officers, fund managers, and departmental heads. Affected venture capital funds were required to ensure compliance and confirm adherence within two months of the circular's issuance on October 18, 2006.

items.title: SEBI amends DIP Guidelines to restrict the benefit of no lock-in for Venture Capital Funds or Foreign Venture Capital Investors
items.summary: SEBI has amended the DIP Guidelines, 2000 to restrict the exemption from lock-in requirements on pre-IPO shares of unlisted companies held by registered Venture Capital Funds and Foreign Venture Capital Investors. Under the updated rules, this no lock-in benefit is now restricted exclusively to shares held for a minimum of one year prior to filing the draft prospectus, and to shares resulting from the conversion of convertible instruments provided the combined holding period of the instrument and shares equals at least one year before the draft prospectus filing date.

items.title: SEBI Board approves (1) guidelines for Real Estate Mutual Funds and (2)Changes in Venture Capital Fund lock- in period for IPOs
items.summary: SEBI introduced regulatory guidelines for Real Estate Mutual Funds, requiring them to operate as close-ended structures with compulsory stock exchange listing, daily NAV disclosures, and property title safekeeping by a registered custodian. Additionally, the Board amended pre-IPO lock-in exemptions for Venture Capital Funds and Foreign Venture Capital Investors, mandating a minimum holding period of one year prior to filing the draft prospectus to qualify for the benefit. These measures apply to mutual funds managing real estate investments and venture capital investors participating in portfolio companies' public offerings, with formal regulatory amendments to be issued separately.

items.title: Registration of Indus Venture Capital Fund -1Orissa Venture Capital Fund and TVS Venture Fund Trust cancelled
items.summary: SEBI has cancelled the registration certificates of three venture capital funds—Indus Venture Capital Fund-1, Orissa Venture Capital Fund, and TVS Venture Fund Trust—following their voluntary notifications regarding fund closure and winding up. Consequently, these entities no longer hold status as SEBI-registered venture capital funds. The cancellations took effect immediately upon the announcement on September 10, 2004.

items.title: cancellation of registration of Uttar Pradesh Venture Capital Fund and Investor Venture Capital fund Trust.
items.summary: SEBI has cancelled the venture capital fund registrations for Uttar Pradesh Venture Capital Fund and iNestor Venture Capital Fund Trust, both based in Mumbai, following their voluntary surrender of the certificates. As a result of this cancellation, effective immediately as of November 29, 2001, these two entities are prohibited from conducting any future venture capital operations under the SEBI (Venture Capital Funds) Regulations, 1996.

items.title: Gazette Notification dated 23/7/2001, Investments by MFs in Venture Capital Funds and Payment of Volatility Margins by MFs
items.summary: This circular and accompanying SEBI (Mutual Funds) Second Amendment Regulations, 2001 apply to all registered mutual funds, Asset Management Companies (AMCs), and Unit Trust of India (UTI). Effective immediately from July 23, 2001, the framework permits mutual fund schemes to invest in venture capital fund securities within existing equity limits, mandates the payment of stock exchange volatility margins on equity sales unless early pay-ins are effected, tightens AMC governance and reporting timelines by requiring directors to file quarterly securities transactions, shortens scheme dispatch windows to 30 days, and accelerates half-yearly financial disclosures to one month alongside a revised reporting format.

items.title: Amendment to SEBI (Venture Capital Funds) Regulations, 1996
items.summary: SEBI amended the Venture Capital Funds Regulations, 1996, effective November 17, 1999, to allow statutory bodies corporate to apply for registration certificates to launch venture capital funds. This change broadens the eligibility criteria specifically for bodies corporate established under specific statutes. The announcement carries no additional timelines or deadlines for compliance beyond the date of the amendment.

items.title: Venture Capital Fund
items.summary: SEBI established a specialized committee headed by Mr. K.B. Chandrasekhar to examine regulatory and developmental bottlenecks in India's venture capital sector and recommend measures to accelerate its growth. The committee applies to key stakeholders across the venture capital ecosystem, including fund managers, financial institutions, legal and tax experts, entrepreneurs, and government representatives. The four newly formed working groups were directed to submit their initial recommendations within six weeks, culminating in a final committee report slated for completion within three months.
